review_candidates.description: Company Description Somaliland Y-PEER is a youth-led, non-profit organisation established in 2008 and legally registered in Somaliland. Headquartered in Hargeisa, the organisation works with communities, government institutions, and development partners to advance young people’s and women’s health, rights, participation, and economic opportunities. With support from the International Solidarity Foundation (ISF) from Finland, Somaliland Y-PEER is implementing the Somaliland Women and Youth Artisans Empowerment Project, which aims to strengthen women’s practical textile, tailoring, and fashion skills and support their transition into employment and self-employment. The Fashion Design and Garment Construction Instructor role contributes directly to this mission by helping women participants develop professional skills in fashion design, garment construction, pattern-making, fitting, and fabric knowledge. Role Description The Fashion Design and Garment Construction Instructor is a full-time, on-site role based at the Project Training Centre in Hargeisa, Somaliland, for an initial period of one year with possible extension. The Instructor will design and deliver practical training on fashion design, fabric knowledge, body measurement, pattern-making, cutting, fitting, sewing, and complete garment construction. Day-to-day responsibilities include preparing lesson plans, demonstrations, practical assignments, visual references, and competency checklists; teaching participants with different literacy levels and prior experience; supervising garment-production exercises; and providing individualized guidance and feedback. The Instructor will teach participants to develop designs that combine contemporary modest fashion with Somali cultural styles and will guide them in producing garments such as abayas, toobs/dresses, dirac, hijabs, skirts, trousers, uniforms, and more advanced garments according to participant competence and available resources. The role also includes assessing participant progress, maintaining learning records, ensuring safe and effective use of tools and equipment, identifying training materials and consumable requirements, and supporting routine equipment care. In addition, the Instructor will work closely with the second technical instructor, business facilitator, project team, and local instructional personnel to coordinate the complete garment-production programme, transfer knowledge, update training content, and maintain training materials, patterns, and assessment resources for continued use by the Centre. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree or recognised advanced technical/vocational qualification in Fashion Design, Fashion and Textile Design, Garment or Apparel Technology, Textile Technology, Clothing and Textile Studies, or a closely related discipline. Minimum 2 years of professional experience in fashion design, pattern-making, cutting, sewing, garment construction, and fitting. Strong practical skills in complete garment construction, including everyday garments and more complex fitted or structured clothing. Advanced competence in pattern-making, cutting, fitting, alterations, and correction of common garment defects. Sound knowledge of fabrics, linings, interfacing, accessories, material selection, and efficient use of materials. Ability to teach fashion sketching, colour coordination, design interpretation, fabric identification, and the development of original designs. Practical understanding of industrial sewing, embroidery, decoration, finishing, pressing, and machinery use sufficient to coordinate effectively with the second technical instructor. Ability to prepare clear lesson plans, demonstrations, practical assignments, competency checklists, and measurable learning outcomes. Previous experience teaching, coaching, supervising, or mentoring learners in tailoring, fashion, garment production, or related fields. Ability to teach beginners and participants with different literacy levels and learning needs using clear, practical, and supportive methods. Strong assessment skills, including the ability to evaluate design interpretation, material selection, measurement, pattern-making, cutting, fitting, garment construction, and overall production quality. Strong communication, teamwork, organisation, and documentation skills, with a commitment to knowledge sharing and coordination with colleagues. Respectful and culturally responsive approach to working with women participants and communities. Sufficient spoken and written English proficiency to prepare training materials, communicate with the project team, and deliver technical instruction in English where required. Teaching qualifications, vocational instructor certification, or training in competency-based education and assessment is an added advantage. Familiarity with the Somaliland context and commitment to women’s economic empowerment, skills development, employment, and self-employment is added adventage. Benefits International applicants selected for the position will be provided with visa support and an economy-class flight ticket to Somaliland. These benefits will be provided in accordance with the project’s applicable arrangements and requirements.
